etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English wantoun, wantowen, wantoȝen, wantowe (“uneducated; unrestrained; licentious; sportive; playful”), from wan- (“not, un-, mis-”) + towen, i-towen (“educated”, literally “towed; led; drawn”), from togen, ġetogen, past participle of tēon (“to train, discipline”), equivalent to wan- +‎ towed.
senses: Undisciplined, unruly; not able to be controlled.
An overly playful person; a trifler.
(intransitive) To rove and ramble without restraint, rule, or limit; to revel; to play loosely; to frolic.
(transitive) To waste or squander, especially in pleasure (most often with away).

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: Borrowed from Cantonese 雲吞 / 云吞 (wan4 tan1).
